newsitem.title: USA: Mattel to issue refund for Cabbage Patch dolls.
newsitem.headline: Mattel to issue refund for Cabbage Patch dolls.

text.p: Toy maker Mattel Inc. said Monday it will offer a $40 refund to owners of its Cabbage Patch Kids Snacktime Kids dolls and discontinue production of the dolls.

In a statement, Mattel said more than 500,000 of the dolls have been sold since the dolls were introduced in the fall of 1996. The safety of the dolls have come under question following 35 cases where the battery operated dolls have chewed up girls' hair.
It was not immediately clear if the toy maker would be forced to take a one-time charge against earnings to pay for the refund programme or how many of the dolls Mattel expected to be returned.

Mattel said the refund followed reports of children getting their hair and fingers caught in the mouths of the dolls. The company said neither it nor the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission had identified a serious safety hazard associated with the dolls in testing.

"Nonetheless, we remain deeply concerned with the satisfaction of all our consumers and in maintaining their long-standing confidence in the safety and value of our toys," said Jill Barad, Mattel's chief executive officer. "Our job is to bring joy to children's lives. If any of our products are causing concerns, we are committed to responding in a responsible manner."
